item.title: Xi, Japarov sign treaty to deepen ties
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-01
Xi, Japarov sign treaty to deepen ties Leaders pledge to boost Sino-Kyrgyz friendship and mutual support At around 11:30 am local time on Monday in Bishkek, the capital of Kyrgyzstan, President Xi Jinping and Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov put their signatures to a treaty on permanent good-neighborliness, friendship and cooperation, after which they exchanged copies of the treaty, shook hands and posed for photographs. The two presidents also signed a joint declaration on the high-quality development of the China-Kyrgyzstan comprehensive strategic partnership for a new era, and witnessed the exchange of bilateral cooperation documents covering investment, transportation, customs and sister-city relations. During Xi's visit, which began on Sunday, the two sides signed more than 20 additional cooperation documents in areas including science and technology, education, culture, people-to-people exchanges and the media. While holding bilateral talks with Japarov, Xi said that high-level political mutual trust and firm mutual support are important guarantees for the steady and long-term development of China-Kyrgyzstan relations. China firmly supports Kyrgyzstan in safeguarding its national sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity, and supports the country in pursuing a development path suited to its national conditions, Xi said. He added that China stands ready to continue firmly supporting Kyrgyzstan on issues concerning each other's core interests. Japarov said he was honored to welcome Xi to Kyrgyzstan on the 35th anniversary of the country's independence, which fell on Monday. The visit further demonstrated the profound friendship and high level of political mutual trust between the two countries and marked an important milestone in bilateral relations, he said. Xi said the signing of the treaty on permanent good-neighborliness, friendship and cooperation will provide an important legal foundation for friendship between the two countries from generation to generation and for their continued mutual support. China is advancing the building of a strong country and national rejuvenation on all fronts through Chinese modernization, while Kyrgyzstan is making every effort to implement its National Development Program through 2030, Xi said. China is ready to work with Kyrgyzstan to better align their development strategies, deepen exchanges of experience in governance and deliver more tangible outcomes through practical cooperation, he said, calling for taking profound and concrete measures in building a China-Kyrgyzstan community with a shared future. Xi called for the two sides to deepen practical cooperation by implementing their intergovernmental economic and trade cooperation plan, diversifying traded goods and fostering new growth drivers such as digital trade and cross-border e-commerce. He called for the high-quality construction of the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway, describing it as a "major transportation artery" carrying the development aspirations of people across the region. The two sides should also modernize border crossings and strengthen "soft connectivity" in institutions, standards and rules, he said. Xi urged more landmark projects in renewable energy and resource recycling, as well as efforts to implement cooperation documents on green minerals and expand collaboration across entire industrial chains. He also called for facilitating personnel exchanges and expanding cooperation among young people, as well as media, tourism, sports, healthcare and subnational exchanges, to further consolidate public support for China-Kyrgyzstan friendship. The two sides should expand law enforcement and security cooperation, jointly combat the "three forces" of terrorism, separatism and extremism, as well as drug trafficking and transnational crime, and work together to safeguard regional peace and stability, Xi said. China supports Kyrgyzstan in playing a greater role in international and regional affairs and is willing to strengthen coordination with the country within the United Nations framework, he said. Xi called on the two countries to jointly implement the four global initiatives, oppose hegemonism and power politics, uphold true multilateralism, safeguard international fairness and justice, and promote a more just and equitable global governance system. As founding members of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization, China and Kyrgyzstan should advance the implementation of the outcomes of last year's Tianjin summit, promote common development in the region and take the SCO's development to a new level, said Xi, who is also in Bishkek for this year's SCO summit. Japarov said the signing of the treaty on permanent good-neighborliness, friendship and cooperation will open up broader prospects for bilateral relations. "The People's Republic of China is an important priority in Kyrgyzstan's foreign policy, and our main trade and investment partner. China is our good neighbor, close friend and time-tested, reliable partner," Japarov told Xi. Japarov also said that Kyrgyzstan is willing to expand cooperation with China in trade and investment, connectivity, scientific and technological innovation, energy, minerals and the green economy, while strengthening exchanges in education, healthcare, culture and youth affairs. Kyrgyzstan is ready to work with China to combat the "three forces" and safeguard regional security, he said. Japarov also expressed his country's willingness to strengthen coordination with China through multilateral platforms, including the UN, the SCO, the China-Central Asia mechanism and the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization. During the talks, Japarov, on behalf of the Kyrgyz government and people, extended his deep sympathies over the mudslide disaster in Gyirong county of China's Xizang autonomous region. Xi thanked him and said the Communist Party of China and the Chinese government are making every effort to search for missing Chinese and foreign nationals, relocate affected residents, treat the injured and guard against secondary disasters. China has also sent rescuers to Nepal and provided emergency assistance, he said. Earlier on Monday morning, Xi and his wife, Peng Liyuan, arrived by car at Yntymak Ordo, the Kyrgyz presidential administration building, under the escort of a Kyrgyz cavalry guard. They were warmly received by Japarov and his wife, Aigul Japarova. mojingxi@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Joint effort sheds light on ancient past
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-01
On the northern bank of the Yassy River beneath the Fergana Mountains, the ruins of Shorobashat in Kyrgyzstan are offering new clues to the region's ancient past, thanks to a joint effort by Chinese and Kyrgyz archaeologists. The collaborative archaeological program at the site was recently launched by the Institute of History, Archaeology and Ethnology of the National Academy of Sciences of the Kyrgyz Republic and the Collaborative Research Center for Archaeology of the Silk Roads, affiliated with Northwest University in Xi'an, Shaanxi province. Located in the eastern Fergana Valley, which stretches across parts of present-day Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan, the site in Kyrgyzstan's Osh region includes a central city spanning about 1.5 square kilometers, two medium-sized cities, tombs, high-platform structures and smaller settlements. This year, the team has begun more detailed exploration. "Building on previous archaeological surveys, we have now begun further explorations using a Luoyang shovel, a traditional curved spade that we insert into the ground and withdraw to examine soil layers, identifying their types and dates. This gives us a clearer picture of the central city's nature, layout, and the preservation of its archaeological features," said Zhang Weixing, the Chinese side's lead archaeologist. The choice of Shorobashat followed extensive preliminary research. Wang Jianxin, chief expert at the Collaborative Research Center for Archaeology of the Silk Roads, said the team's approach to Central Asian archaeology combines large-scale regional surveys with small-scale, targeted excavations. Since 2023, during the first phase of the project, archaeologists have surveyed more than 500 sites, including cities, high-platform structures and tombs. They have carefully documented each site through observation, mapping, measuring, and photography. Based on this extensive body of data, the team selected Shorobashat for further exploration. No systematic archaeological research had been conducted at the site for about seven decades. This year, the archaeologists have examined the city walls, tower structures, gates and roads, while identifying key areas for future excavation. Zhang said the team has drawn up a five-year plan and will continue its work at the site in the years ahead. He said the research forms part of a broader effort to understand the Fergana Valley before the 7th century, when the region maintained close ties with ancient China. Chinese historical records offer clues to the location of Dayuan, an important Hellenistic state in Central Asia that existed during the Han Dynasty (206 BC-AD 220). According to Zhang, Chinese records mention three major cities in Dayuan: its capital, Guishan; Ershi, a major horse-breeding hub; and Yucheng, located in eastern Dayuan. Based on textual analysis, the Shorobashat site is generally believed to be associated with the ancient city of Yucheng. "We pay special attention to the historical development of Dayuan, its material culture, people's thoughts and beliefs, and its role along the ancient Silk Road ... We also want to trace the valley's civilizational progress during the prehistoric period," said Zhang. The Northwest University team's involvement in Fergana Valley archaeology dates back to 2019, when Wang invited scholars from Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan to Xi'an for a seminar on archaeological research in the valley. The meeting led to an agreement on future multilateral cooperation. "Many Central Asian scholars have a strong sense of responsibility toward their cultural heritage," said Zhang. "For example, Kyrgyz scholars played a big role in the application for World Heritage status for 'Silk Roads: the Routes Network of Chang'an-Tianshan Corridor' in 2014. "On this project, we work side by side, communicating constantly, with a shared goal: to identify significant sites, protect them, and eventually present them to the public. That common purpose and the friendship it has fostered have brought us together."

item.title: RV life blooming in Guizhou campground
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-01
RV life blooming in Guizhou campground Springtime rhododendrons, community life and cool climate attract seasonal visitors including retirees and families Cucumbers climb from a planter, and freshly brewed coffee fills the air. Li Qun steps outside to greet her neighbors. It feels like a small neighborhood, with gardens, tables and people lingering outside. But there are no houses here. The homes are parked on wheels. Starting in April, hundreds of RVs have rolled into Baili Dujuan, Bijie, Guizhou province, turning parking lots here into seasonal communities. Average temperatures hover around 19 C, drawing retirees, families and long-term travelers seeking relief from the heat. Some stay just a few days at this springtime rhododendron destination. Many stay for months. Around Li's RV, flowers and vegetables fill recycled containers. A small table and low stools spill into the parking space. Li arrived in June, and in many ways, she said, the campground now feels like home. Li, from Sichuan province, first visited in 2021. Now nearing 60 and retired after working in the construction industry, she has been traveling around China in a recreational vehicle with her husband on a 10-year journey. She returned the following year in her own RV and began recommending the destination to fellow RV enthusiasts. Word spread, and the campground gradually filled with seasonal residents. "I've visited almost all the attractions nearby," Li said. "Now I just enjoy staying here quietly." Sometimes she makes liangfen, a chilled starch jelly that is a specialty of her hometown, and sells it to her neighbors. "I'm not doing this to make money," she said. "When I'm in the mood, I just make a few bowls." When villagers bring her fresh vegetables, she always makes a few extra bowls to share with friends. Around her, other RV owners have made their parking spaces their own. They grow vegetables, cook meals and visit neighbors from across China. At Baili Dujuan, everyday life is simple and social. New arrivals often get help from their temporary neighbors to pitch awnings and tents, then make the space their own with flowers, potted plants and even karaoke machines. RV groups and word of mouth have helped turn the campground into a thriving community of travelers who stay for weeks or months. Residents head to local markets, pick up fresh produce, cook meals and visit one another. When the summer break begins, children also join their parents on the road. "Everyone here feels like a neighbor," said Chen Yan, the site manager. During the peak season, the campground also holds communal banquets, bonfire parties and performances. The peak season usually runs from May through September. Some visitors arrive as early as April to see the rhododendrons, then decide to stay after experiencing the cool weather. Daily parking fees range from 10 to 68 yuan ($1.48 to 10.10), depending on the space and access to utilities. But the climate is the main draw. Luo Ji, deputy director of the Baili Dujuan culture and tourism bureau, said summer temperatures average about 19 C. Surrounded by forests, the area also has relatively high levels of negative oxygen ions, which can support respiratory and circulatory health. For city dwellers looking to escape the heat, he said, it is like a "natural air conditioner". Mao Jingbo, from Zhejiang province, came for much the same reason. The 39-year-old arrived with her young daughter and now runs the campground's only permanent coffee shop. An avid RV traveler who has toured places including the Xinjiang Uygur autonomous region, Mao said Baili Dujuan remains her favorite summer destination. The heat in her hometown makes it difficult to take her daughter outdoors. Here, she can simply step outside the RV and let her daughter play. On a good day, Mao sells 15 or 16 cups of coffee. On a quiet day, she may sell only one or two. Mao, a devoted coffee lover, said she sees making a good cup of coffee as a pleasure in itself. "I don't worry about how much I make each day," she said. "As long as I can cover the campground fee, that's good enough." Chen estimated that about 42 percent stay for three to four months, while others remain for one to two months or even four to five months. Only about 10 percent stay less than a month. Together, they have created a seasonal community that moves with the weather. When temperatures drop in late September, many pack up and head south to Yunnan province, the Guangxi Zhuang autonomous region or Hainan province. Their RVs become homes on the move, carrying them from one comfortable season to the next. For some, the good life is not complicated: an RV, a few pots of vegetables, a cup of coffee and a long summer afternoon with nowhere else to be.

item.title: CXMT surging forward in memory race
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-01
CXMT surging forward in memory race Chinese chipmaker's DRAM to debut in Xiaomi's upcoming foldable Chinese memory-chip maker ChangXin Memory Technologies is moving closer to a vanguard position amid the global DRAM race with one of the earliest commercial deployments of LPDDR6 in a flagship smartphone, industry experts said on Monday. They made the comments as CXMT said on Saturday that it had begun mass production of its self-developed LPDDR6 DRAM, which will debut in Xiaomi's upcoming 18 Fold handset. The chip has a peak data-transfer rate of 12,800 megabits per second and capacity of up to 16 gigabytes. "For a Chinese company that only began mass-producing its first DRAM products in 2019, the bigger significance is not simply being first with one product," said Wang Peng, a researcher at the Beijing Academy of Social Sciences. "It put CXMT into the first wave of competition around the latest mobile-memory standard alongside global heavyweights Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix and Micron Technology," Wang said. LPDDR6 is designed to raise memory bandwidth and parallelism while cutting power consumption, with these features becoming increasingly important as artificial intelligence models migrate from cloud data centers into phones, PCs, cars and other modalities. The Xiaomi partnership adds another dimension. It puts a Chinese-designed mobile processor and the country's newest-generation DRAM together inside a premium smartphone. Xiaomi founder and CEO Lei Jun said the company's Xring O3 would support CXMT's LPDDR6, and he expects deeper collaboration among Chinese tech companies. Advanced chips require years of engineering but also large-scale customer validation to improve yields, reliability and costs. China's huge base of smartphone, computer, electric vehicle and internet companies can give local chipmakers something laboratory breakthroughs alone cannot provide — millions of devices on which new technology can be tested and refined, industry experts said. Liu Zhiying, a professor at the University of Science and Technology of China, said, "An important factor in the growth of Chinese high-tech companies is their ability to connect research, commercialization and market applications, allowing leading companies to pull suppliers across the industrial chain forward." CXMT's technological progress is arriving alongside a dramatic expansion in its financial firepower. On Monday, shares of CXMT closed at 58.01 yuan ($8.6), down 1.01 percent on the day, valuing the company at about 3.94 trillion yuan and making it one of China's most valuable listed companies. The company recently reported first-half revenue of 150.31 billion yuan, up about 874 percent from a year earlier, while net profit attributable to shareholders reached 77.61 billion yuan, reversing a 2.33 billion yuan loss a year earlier. The surge was driven by sharply higher memory prices and rising sales as demand for computing power tightened global DRAM supplies, the company said. CXMT has grown into the world's fourth-largest DRAM producer, behind Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix and Micron, turning China from a marginal player in memory chips into an increasingly consequential competitor. Last week, CXMT sued the US Department of Defense in federal court in Washington, seeking removal from a Pentagon list of companies alleged to have ties to China's military. CXMT said its chips are designed primarily for civilian and commercial use and that it has no affiliation with the Chinese military. It said the designation was unsupported by facts and had damaged its reputation and business interests since it was first placed on the Pentagon's blacklist in January 2025. The lawsuit follows similar legal challenges by Chinese companies including Xiaomi and WuXi AppTec. Xiaomi successfully challenged an earlier Pentagon military designation in 2021. Zhang Sinan, an independent commentator who has been following the situation, said, "The US can keep extending the list, but the world will not stop needing cheaper clean energy, more efficient electric vehicles, more advanced drug development services or more flexible robotic applications simply because of a list." chengyu@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Medical mission restores sight to over 1,400 patients
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-01
Medical mission restores sight to over 1,400 patients 'Lifeline Express' initiative helps locals regain vision while training physicians A Chinese medical initiative has performed 1,478 free cataract surgeries in Kyrgyzstan as part of an ongoing health aid program, according to figures released by health authorities. During the project's fourth deployment to the country, held from May 15 to 26, an 11-member specialist team from the People's Hospital of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region completed 321 surgical procedures. Each operation utilized a four-doctor rotation covering preoperative preparation, performing the procedure, postoperative checks and follow-up care, with average procedure times reported at under 15 minutes. China has been sending medical aid and equipment to Kyrgyzstan for decades through the Shanghai Cooperation Organization framework to help shore up gaps in healthcare in underserved areas. The latest medical mission forms part of China's "Lifeline Express" initiative, organized jointly by the National Health Commission's International Health Exchange and Cooperation Center and the Chinese Foundation for Lifeline Express. In addition to cataract treatments, program organizers report the initiative has funded 35 glaucoma and 30 retinal surgeries in the region. One patient, a 74-year-old retired typist, said she had lost all vision in one eye because of cataracts. "They performed a free surgery on me, and even the medication was free of charge," she was quoted by local media outlet New Silk Road Observer as saying. Following the procedure, she said she was excited to discover that she could once again distinguish colors effortlessly and even read tiny, densely printed text. Beyond direct clinical care, the project established a blindness-prevention cooperation center at the Interstate United Clinical Hospital in Osh, Kyrgyzstan. The venue serves as a hub for local physician training programs and academic exchanges between Chinese and Kyrgyz medical personnel. At a bilateral meeting in late June, Zheng Zhe, vice-minister of China's National Health Commission, met with Kyrgyz counterparts to discuss expanding health sector initiatives. Zheng expressed intent to scale similar targeted medical programs as part of broader regional health cooperation, according to a statement from the commission. He said China is willing to deepen bilateral healthcare cooperation by implementing more small-scale but well-targeted projects like the eye care initiative, promoting greater exchanges between medical professionals on both sides, so as to contribute to building a global community of health for all. wangxiaoyu@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Peng visits Kyrgyz historical museum
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-01
Peng visits Kyrgyz historical museum China and Kyrgyzstan attach great importance to preserving and passing on traditional culture, Peng Liyuan, wife of President Xi Jinping, said on Monday, as she expressed hope that the two nations will continue to expand people-to-people exchanges and further enhance mutual understanding between their two peoples. Peng made the remarks when visiting the National Historical Museum of the Kyrgyz Republic in Bishkek, the capital of the Central Asian country, with Aigul Japarova, wife of Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov. During the visit, Peng and Japarova watched a welcoming performance together, and then appreciated an exhibition on traditional Kyrgyz culture. The costumes, carpets and other items on display are exquisitely crafted and richly colored, reflecting the Kyrgyz people's long-standing handicraft traditions and unique customs, Peng said. They also visited an art exhibition on ancient Chinese civilization and watched a Kyrgyz ethnic costume show, where they both expressed willingness to promote cultural exchanges and mutual learning between the two countries. The three-month exhibition, titled "Harmony Creates Beauty: An Art Exhibition of Ancient Chinese Civilization", opened on Aug 18 at the National Historical Museum. It features 153 exhibits from China's Tianjin Museum and Inner Mongolia Museum, as well as from the Kyrgyz museum. The National Historical Museum of the Kyrgyz Republic is the highest-level national museum in Kyrgyzstan, housing a collection of artifacts that traces the history and development of the Kyrgyz people. zhoujin@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Consolidating mutual trust with Mongolia stressed
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-01
Consolidating mutual trust with Mongolia stressed President Xi Jinping called on China and Mongolia to consolidate strategic mutual trust, deepen mutually beneficial cooperation and strengthen the bonds between their peoples, during a meeting with Mongolian President Ukhnaa Khurelsukh in Bishkek, the capital of Kyrgyzstan, on Monday. The two sides should inject greater vitality into their comprehensive strategic partnership and advance the building of a China-Mongolia community with a shared future, Xi said. Peaceful coexistence, mutual support and win-win cooperation have always been the defining features of bilateral relations, Xi said, adding that China will continue to place ties with Mongolia high on the agenda of its neighborhood diplomacy. Xi stressed the need for the two countries to consolidate the political foundation of their relationship, and respect each other's independence, sovereignty and territorial integrity. Xi also called on the two sides to strengthen coordination and collaboration in multilateral affairs and jointly address global challenges. Khurelsukh said that deepening friendly cooperation with China is a top priority of Mongolia's foreign policy, while reaffirming his country's firm commitment to the one-China principle. Mongolia is willing to work with China to advance the vision of building a community with a shared future for humanity, he added.

item.title: Relationship with Uzbekistan ushers in 'golden decade'
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-01
Relationship with Uzbekistan ushers in 'golden decade' President Xi Jinping expressed on Monday China's readiness to work with Uzbekistan to consolidate strategic mutual trust, deepen mutually beneficial cooperation and usher in a new "golden decade" for bilateral relations. Xi made the remarks during a meeting with Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev in Bishkek, the capital of Kyrgyzstan. This year marks the 10th anniversary of the China-Uzbekistan comprehensive strategic partnership. Xi emphasized the improvement and upgrading of bilateral ties, the fruitful outcomes of bilateral cooperation in various areas, and the achievements in the building of the China-Uzbekistan community with a shared future. He called on the two countries to advance the high-quality construction of the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway, expand cooperation in artificial intelligence and desertification control, and pursue win-win outcomes. As founding members of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization, China and Uzbekistan should work together to implement the outcomes of last year's Tianjin summit and promote regional development and prosperity, he added. Mirziyoyev said that Uzbekistan is firmly committed to developing relations with China and stands ready to work with China to deepen political mutual trust, expand trade and investment, and promote people-to-people exchanges. zhoujin@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Momentum of strong ties with Russia hailed
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-01
Momentum of strong ties with Russia hailed Exchanges and cooperation between China and Russia have maintained a dynamic momentum of development, President Xi Jinping said on Monday when meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan. In May, Putin made a successful state visit to China. Xi noted that he and Putin had made arrangements from a strategic, long-term perspective to take bilateral relations to a higher quality and a higher level of development. They also reached consensus on deepening cooperation across various fields under new circumstances. Both countries' relevant authorities are actively implementing the consensus and have already achieved many outcomes, Xi said. He expressed confidence that under their strategic guidance and through joint efforts, the foundation of the relationship will become more solid, progress will be steadier, and prospects will be brighter. Putin noted that bilateral cooperation has developed rapidly. Russia is willing to maintain high-level exchanges with China, strengthen cooperation in areas such as trade, energy, industry, transportation, and science and technology, and enhance people-to-people exchanges, he said. Speaking on the international situation, Xi said currently changes unseen in a century are accelerating, and uncertainties and unforeseeable factors in the international landscape have markedly increased. However, pursuit of peace, development, cooperation and win-win outcomes by peoples around the world remains unchanged, he said. The SCO shoulders the mission of maintaining regional stability and promoting development, he said. Putin said Russia and China should continuously strengthen unity and cooperation within the SCO and play a leading role.

item.title: 25 Years of the SCO: Building a Shared Future
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-30
25 Years of the SCO: Building a Shared Future Share - WeChat
President Xi Jinping once said, "The Shanghai Spirit has inspired a strong sense of solidarity which ensures the growth of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization." Twenty-five years on, that spirit continues to guide the organization on the road toward a shared future with deeper cooperation and stronger global governance.
